_readme: WORKSHEETS BY GRADE - the hub page, plus Grade 6 and Grade 7.
Grades 8 and 9 are in worksheets-8-9.json, Grades 10 and 11 in worksheets-10-11.json.
Every worksheet on these pages was WRITTEN FOR RCF ENGLISH. No passage,
exercise or answer key is copied from a textbook, a workbook or another
website. That is what allows them to be published and freely copied for
Each grade page carries ten worksheets: four grammar, three reading and
three writing. Each one states its focus, gives the task, and ends with an
answer key so a teacher can mark it without preparing anything.

blocks.heading: How to use these
text: Every worksheet states what it practises, gives the task, and ends with the answers. Nothing needs preparing: open the page, read the task to the class or copy it onto the board, and mark it from the key.
They are arranged by grade, but the grade is a guide and not a rule. A Grade 9 class that has not met reported speech should do the Grade 8 sheet on it first.

hero.text: Ten worksheets for Grade 6: four grammar, three reading and three writing, each with the answers.

a: **Focus:** telling a common noun from a proper noun, and using capital letters correctly.
**Task A.** Underline the nouns and write C for common or P for proper above each one.
1. Kamal went to Kandy on Monday. 2. My sister keeps a rabbit. 3. We crossed the Mahaweli river. 4. The teacher opened the window. 5. Nimali reads the Daily News every morning.
**Task B.** Rewrite each sentence with the capital letters put right.
6. we visited galle in april. 7. my brother studies at ananda college. 8. the shop on temple road sells bread. 9. sri lanka is an island. 10. mrs perera teaches english.

**Answers.** A: 1. Kamal (P), Kandy (P), Monday (P) 2. sister (C), rabbit (C) 3. Mahaweli (P), river (C) 4. teacher (C), window (C) 5. Nimali (P), Daily News (P), morning (C). B: 6. We visited Galle in April. 7. My brother studies at Ananda College. 8. The shop on Temple Road sells bread. 9. Sri Lanka is an island. 10. Mrs Perera teaches English.

items.q: Worksheet 2 — Verbs: is, are, was, were
a: **Focus:** matching the verb to a singular or plural subject, in present and past.
**Task A.** Fill in *is* or *are*.
1. The boy ____ hungry. 2. My shoes ____ new. 3. There ____ a bird on the roof. 4. The children ____ in the garden. 5. Rice and curry ____ my favourite meal.
**Task B.** Fill in *was* or *were*.
6. The market ____ crowded yesterday. 7. We ____ late for school. 8. She ____ very kind to me. 9. The books ____ on the shelf. 10. It ____ raining all night.
**Answers.** 1. is 2. are 3. is 4. are 5. is 6. was 7. were 8. was 9. were 10. was.
**Teaching note.** Question 5 catches many children: *rice and curry* is treated as one dish, so the verb is singular. Accept *are* if the child can explain that they mean two separate things.
**Focus:** choosing the right article, including *an* before a vowel sound.
**Task A.** Fill in *a* or *an*.
1. ____ elephant 2. ____ book 3. ____ hour 4. ____ umbrella 5. ____ university 6. ____ orange 7. ____ house 8. ____ honest man
**Task B.** Fill in *a*, *an* or *the*.
9. I saw ____ cat. ____ cat was black. 10. She is ____ best student in ____ class. 11. My father bought ____ old bicycle. 12. Please shut ____ door.
**Answers.** 1. an 2. a 3. an 4. an 5. a 6. an 7. a 8. an 9. a / The 10. the / the 11. an 12. the.
**Teaching note.** 3, 5 and 8 are the ones to spend time on. It is the *sound*, not the letter: *hour* begins with a vowel sound, *university* begins with a *y* sound.

items.q: Worksheet 4 — Prepositions of place and time
a: **Focus:** in, on, at, under, between, behind — for place and for time.
**Task A.** Fill in the correct preposition of place.
1. The cat is ____ the table (below it). 2. The picture hangs ____ the wall. 3. She sat ____ Amal and Nimal. 4. The keys are ____ my bag. 5. He hid ____ the door.
**Task B.** Fill in *in*, *on* or *at* for time.
6. School starts ____ 7.30. 7. We go to the temple ____ Sunday. 8. My birthday is ____ May. 9. It is cold ____ the morning. 10. The bus leaves ____ night.
**Answers.** 1. under 2. on 3. between 4. in 5. behind 6. at 7. on 8. in 9. in 10. at.

**Teaching note.** For time the rule is worth writing on the board: **at** a clock time, **on** a day or date, **in** a month, year or part of the day. *At night* is the exception, and children remember it better if you call it that.
**Focus:** finding facts stated directly in a short passage.

**Passage.** *A new pupil joined our class on Tuesday. Her name is Dilini and she came from a school in Matara. She sat beside me because the seat next to mine was empty. At the interval she showed me a photograph of her dog. By the end of the day she knew everybody's name.*

**Questions.** 1. When did the new pupil join? 2. What is her name? 3. Which town did she come from? 4. Why did she sit beside the writer? 5. What did she show at the interval? 6. What had she done by the end of the day?
**Answers.** 1. On Tuesday. 2. Dilini. 3. Matara. 4. Because the seat next to the writer was empty. 5. A photograph of her dog. 6. She knew everybody's name.
**Marking note.** Insist on full sentences. *She joined on Tuesday* earns the mark; *Tuesday* is the right answer badly written, and this is the year to fix that.
**Focus:** sequence — putting events in the order they happened.

**Passage.** *The lights went out just as we sat down to eat. My father found the torch, but the battery was flat. My mother lit two candles instead. We ate by candlelight, and my little brother said it was better than a birthday party. The lights came back an hour later.*

**Questions.** 1. What happened first? 2. Why was the torch no use? 3. What did the mother do? 4. What did the brother say? 5. How long were the lights off? 6. Number these in order: *the candles were lit / the lights went out / the lights came back / the torch did not work.*

**Answers.** 1. The lights went out as they sat down to eat. 2. The battery was flat. 3. She lit two candles. 4. That it was better than a birthday party. 5. About an hour. 6. the lights went out (1), the torch did not work (2), the candles were lit (3), the lights came back (4).
**Marking note.** Question 6 is the one that matters. A child who can order events can retell a story, and retelling in order is the base of every summary they will ever write.
**Focus:** working out a word from the sentence around it.

**Passage.** *Every morning an old man pushes his cart to the corner of our lane and sells mangoes. His voice is hoarse from calling out all day, but he never stops smiling. Yesterday a boy took a mango without paying. The old man saw him, said nothing, and let him go.*

**Questions.** 1. Where does the old man stop? 2. What does he sell? 3. What does *hoarse* mean here — sweet, rough, or loud? Which words in the passage helped you decide? 4. What did the boy do? 5. What did the old man do about it? 6. What kind of person is the old man? Give one reason from the passage.

**Answers.** 1. At the corner of the writer's lane. 2. Mangoes. 3. Rough. *From calling out all day* is the clue. 4. He took a mango without paying. 5. Nothing — he said nothing and let the boy go. 6. Accept any reasonable answer with evidence: kind or forgiving, because he let the boy go; or cheerful, because he never stops smiling.
**Marking note.** In question 3 the reason is worth more than the word. A child who guesses *rough* without the clue has not done the exercise.
**Focus:** capital letter, word order, full stop.
**Task A.** Put the words in order and write the sentence correctly.
1. school / to / walk / I / every / day 2. garden / the / playing / are / children / in / the 3. is / my / a / mother / teacher 4. rained / it / night / all 5. bag / where / my / is
**Task B.** Rewrite each line with the capital letter and full stop or question mark put right.
6. the dog barked loudly 7. do you like mangoes 8. we went to colombo on friday 9. what is your name 10. my brother can swim

**Answers.** A: 1. I walk to school every day. 2. The children are playing in the garden. 3. My mother is a teacher. 4. It rained all night. 5. Where is my bag? B: 6. The dog barked loudly. 7. Do you like mangoes? 8. We went to Colombo on Friday. 9. What is your name? 10. My brother can swim.
**Focus:** writing five linked sentences about one person.
**Task.** Write five sentences about someone in your family. Use one sentence for each of these, in this order:
1. Who they are and their name. 2. What they look like. 3. What they do each day. 4. One thing they are good at. 5. Why you like them.

**Model answer.** *My grandmother's name is Somawathie. She is small and thin, and her hair is completely white. Every morning she waters the plants before anyone else wakes up. She is very good at making string hoppers. I like her because she never shouts, even when I break something.*

**Marking guide.** One mark for each of the five points covered; one mark for capital letters and full stops throughout; one mark for the sentences being about the same person all the way through. Six marks in all.
**Teaching note.** Do not accept a list. The point of the exercise is five *sentences*, each one complete.

items.q: Worksheet 10 — A short paragraph: my morning
a: **Focus:** joining sentences into one paragraph using *first, then, after that, finally*.
**Task.** Write one paragraph of six to eight sentences describing your morning from waking up to reaching school. Use *first*, *then*, *after that* and *finally* at least once each.

**Model answer.** *I wake up at half past five, when it is still dark. First I wash my face and brush my teeth. Then I put on my uniform and polish my shoes. After that I eat breakfast, which is usually bread and tea. My mother checks my bag while I eat. Finally I walk to the junction and catch the school bus. I reach school just before half past seven.*

**Marking guide.** Two marks for using all four linking words correctly; two marks for the events being in a sensible order; two marks for capital letters and full stops; two marks for staying on the topic. Eight marks in all.
**Teaching note.** Children often use *then* five times. Reading the model aloud and asking them to count the different linking words fixes this faster than telling them.

hero.text: Ten worksheets for Grade 7: four grammar, three reading and three writing, each with the answers.

items.q: Worksheet 1 — Simple present and present continuous
a: **Focus:** what happens usually against what is happening now.
**Task A.** Put the verb in the simple present or the present continuous.

1. My father ____ (read) the newspaper every morning. 2. Look! The baby ____ (cry). 3. Water ____ (boil) at 100 degrees. 4. She ____ (wear) a red dress today. 5. We ____ (go) to the temple on Poya days.
**Task B.** Correct the mistake in each sentence.
6. I am knowing the answer. 7. He play cricket every Saturday. 8. They are wanting more time. 9. She is going to school by bus every day. 10. The sun is rising in the east.

**Answers.** A: 1. reads 2. is crying 3. boils 4. is wearing 5. go. B: 6. I know the answer. 7. He plays cricket every Saturday. 8. They want more time. 9. She goes to school by bus every day. 10. The sun rises in the east.

**Teaching note.** 6 and 8 are the useful ones: *know* and *want* are not normally used in the continuous. Give the class three more such verbs — *like*, *believe*, *understand* — and ask for sentences.
**Focus:** -er and -est, more and most, and the irregular forms.
**Task A.** Write the comparative and superlative.
1. tall 2. happy 3. beautiful 4. good 5. bad 6. thin 7. expensive 8. little
**Task B.** Complete each sentence.
9. An elephant is ____ (big) than a buffalo. 10. This is the ____ (interesting) book I have read. 11. My handwriting is ____ (bad) than yours. 12. Kandy is ____ (cool) than Colombo.

**Answers.** A: 1. taller, tallest 2. happier, happiest 3. more beautiful, most beautiful 4. better, best 5. worse, worst 6. thinner, thinnest 7. more expensive, most expensive 8. less, least. B: 9. bigger 10. most interesting 11. worse 12. cooler.
**Teaching note.** The doubling rule in 6 (thin, thinner) is worth stating: one short vowel and one final consonant, so the consonant doubles.

items.q: Worksheet 3 — Plurals, including the awkward ones
a: **Focus:** the regular rules first, then the exceptions worth memorising.
**Task A.** Write the plural.
1. box 2. baby 3. leaf 4. tooth 5. child 6. potato 7. key 8. knife 9. sheep 10. woman
**Task B.** Correct the mistake.
11. I have three childs. 12. The mans are working. 13. She bought two loafs of bread. 14. There are many mouses in the store. 15. He lost both his tooths.
**Answers.** A: 1. boxes 2. babies 3. leaves 4. teeth 5. children 6. potatoes 7. keys 8. knives 9. sheep 10. women. B: 11. children 12. men 13. loaves 14. mice 15. teeth.
**Teaching note.** Contrast 2 (baby, babies) with 7 (key, keys). The rule is about the letter before the *y*: a consonant changes it to *-ies*, a vowel does not.
**Focus:** joining two short sentences into one, and choosing the right joining word.
**Task A.** Join each pair using the word in brackets.

1. It was raining. We stayed at home. (so) 2. She is clever. She is lazy. (but) 3. I was late. The bus broke down. (because) 4. He washed the car. He cleaned the windows. (and) 5. The shop was closed. We came back later. (so)
**Task B.** Fill in *and*, *but*, *because* or *so*.

6. I like mangoes ____ I do not like papaw. 7. He ran fast ____ he still missed the bus. 8. She stayed at home ____ she was ill. 9. The film was long ____ boring. 10. It was very hot, ____ we sat under the tree.

**Answers.** A: 1. It was raining, so we stayed at home. 2. She is clever but she is lazy. 3. I was late because the bus broke down. 4. He washed the car and cleaned the windows. 5. The shop was closed, so we came back later. B: 6. but 7. but 8. because 9. and 10. so.
**Teaching note.** *Because* answers *why*; *so* gives the result. Ask the class which of the two comes before the reason and which after, and let them work it out from question 3 and question 5.
**Focus:** finding facts, and one question that needs two pieces of information joined.

**Passage.** *Our school library opens at eight and closes at three, except on Fridays, when it closes at noon. Each pupil may borrow two books at a time and must return them within a fortnight. A book kept longer costs five rupees a day. Last term Sanduni forgot a book for six days.*

**Questions.** 1. What time does the library open? 2. When does it close on Fridays? 3. How many books may a pupil borrow? 4. How long may a book be kept? 5. How much did Sanduni have to pay? 6. If you borrowed a book on the first of the month, when would it be due?
**Answers.** 1. At eight. 2. At noon. 3. Two. 4. A fortnight, which is two weeks. 5. Thirty rupees, because six days at five rupees a day. 6. On the fifteenth.
**Marking note.** Questions 5 and 6 are the point of the sheet. Both need the child to combine two facts rather than copy one.
**Focus:** working out what is not stated — inference.

**Passage.** *Ranjan checked the tyres twice before he set off, although he had pumped them the night before. He had folded the map into his shirt pocket, and he touched it every few minutes as he rode. When he reached the top of the hill he stopped, looked back at the town, and only then began to whistle.*

**Questions.** 1. What had Ranjan done the night before? 2. Where did he keep the map? 3. Why do you think he checked the tyres twice? 4. Why did he keep touching his pocket? 5. Why did he not whistle until he reached the top? 6. How do you think he felt at the start of the journey, and how did that change?

**Answers.** 1. He had pumped the tyres. 2. Folded into his shirt pocket. 3. Accept: he was anxious, or he wanted to be sure nothing would go wrong. 4. To check the map was still there — again, anxiety. 5. Accept: he was concentrating, or nervous, until the hardest part was over. 6. Nervous or worried at the start, relieved or pleased at the top. The whistling is the evidence.
**Marking note.** No answer from 3 onwards is stated in the passage. Any sensible answer supported by the text earns the mark; an answer with no support does not, however sensible it sounds.
**Focus:** reading for specific information and comparing two short texts.
**Notice A.** *SCHOOL SPORTS MEET. Saturday 14th June, 8.00 a.m. at the school grounds. All pupils of Grades 6 to 9. Bring water and a hat. Parents are welcome.*
**Notice B.** *INTER-HOUSE DEBATE. Friday 20th June, 1.30 p.m. in the main hall. Grades 8 to 11 only. Entry by house ticket. No latecomers will be admitted.*

**Questions.** 1. Which event is in the morning? 2. Which grades may attend both events? 3. What must you bring to the sports meet? 4. What do you need to enter the debate? 5. Which event may parents attend? 6. A Grade 7 pupil wants to attend both. Can she? Explain.

**Answers.** 1. The sports meet. 2. Grades 8 and 9. 3. Water and a hat. 4. A house ticket. 5. The sports meet. 6. No. She may attend the sports meet, because Grade 7 is within Grades 6 to 9, but not the debate, which is Grades 8 to 11 only.
**Marking note.** Question 6 needs both halves. Half an answer earns half the marks, and it is worth saying so before they start.
**Focus:** the four things every notice must contain.
**Task.** Your class is holding a book sale to raise money for the library. Write a notice of about 40 words. It must give: **what** is happening, **when**, **where**, and **who** may come.

**Model answer.** *BOOK SALE. The Grade 7 class is holding a book sale to raise money for the school library. It will be held on Wednesday 9th July from 10.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. in the Grade 7 classroom. All pupils and parents are welcome. Books from twenty rupees.*
**Marking guide.** One mark each for what, when, where and who; one mark for a heading in capitals; one mark for staying near 40 words. Six marks.
**Teaching note.** Ask the class to check a partner's notice against the four questions before handing it in. They find each other's missing information much faster than they find their own.
**Focus:** ordering a description, and using the senses.
**Task.** Write two paragraphs of about 50 words each describing the market in your town. In the first paragraph write what you **see**. In the second write what you **hear and smell**.

**Model answer.** *The market opens onto a narrow street lined with wooden stalls. Baskets of red onions, green chillies and yellow limes are stacked so high that the sellers are almost hidden behind them. A row of bicycles leans against the wall, and above everything hangs a torn blue awning that lets the sun through in patches.*

*The noise begins before you arrive: sellers calling their prices, a radio somewhere playing too loudly, and the constant ring of bicycle bells. The smell changes as you walk. Near the entrance it is dried fish. In the middle it is coriander and cut ginger. At the far end, where the flowers are, it is suddenly sweet.*

**Marking guide.** Two marks for the paragraph division being kept properly; three marks for detail that is specific rather than general; two marks for accurate sentences; one mark for length. Eight marks.
**Teaching note.** *It was very nice* earns nothing. Push for the particular: which vegetables, which smell, which sound.
**Focus:** the imperative, and putting steps in a workable order.
**Task.** Write instructions telling someone how to make a cup of tea. Use six to eight steps. Begin each step with a verb, and use *first, next, then, after that, finally*.

**Model answer.** *First, fill the kettle with fresh water and switch it on. Next, put one teaspoon of tea leaves into the pot. When the water boils, pour it over the leaves. Then cover the pot and leave it for three minutes. After that, pour the tea through a strainer into a cup. Add milk and sugar to taste. Finally, stir well and serve at once.*

**Marking guide.** Two marks for every step beginning with a verb; two marks for the steps being in a workable order; two marks for at least four different linking words; two marks for accurate sentences. Eight marks.

**Teaching note.** The test of this exercise is whether the steps actually work. Read one aloud and follow it exactly, including the mistakes. A class that watches you pour boiling water into an empty pot will never forget the order again.
